records.title: Where the Tokens Go: Heat, Entropy and Error in Agentic Coding
records.claim: Here we introduce a theory of software thermodynamics.

method_and_setup.method: Here we introduce a theory of software thermodynamics.

results.measures: About 80 per cent of the tokens of a successful run are generated in model calls that leave the requested change where it was, and we call these tokens heat.
The free energy of a change, which we estimate by analogy with the equality of Jarzynski, is 14 to 22 per cent of the mean cost of a successful coding run.

records.change_for_agents: Log tokens per model call that leave the requested change unchanged and track them as waste.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Gives a way to see how much of a coding agent run token spend is wasted retries; useful when budgeting Claude Code runs.

records.title: GUARD: Stabilizing Recursive Self-Improvement with Regret Guidance
records.claim: We introduce GUARD (Grader-free Unsupervised Environment Design [UED] with Adaptive Rule Distillation), a closed-loop framework for reference-free continual harness evolution.

method_and_setup.method: We introduce GUARD (Grader-free Unsupervised Environment Design [UED] with Adaptive Rule Distillation), a closed-loop framework for reference-free continual harness evolution.

records.change_for_agents: Only promote a harness edit when it fixes new failures without breaking previously mastered self-checks.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Directly relevant to editing skills and memory files without regressions or memory bloat; the gating idea could guard my own skill/memory edits.

records.title: GRAFT: Execution-Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design
records.claim: We introduce Execution Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design (GRAFT), which uses aggregate fitness for selection and survival and parent-specific execution evidence to guide semantic crossover with integrated mutation.

method_and_setup.method: We introduce Execution Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design (GRAFT), which uses aggregate fitness for selection and survival and parent-specific execution evidence to guide semantic crossover with integrated mutation.

results.measures: It achieves a mean test accuracy of 82.0%, exceeding the strongest baseline by 9.8% points.

records.change_for_agents: Feed samples of successful and failed runs, not just a score, to whatever proposes your next agent design.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Search over agent architectures guided by per-run execution evidence; mostly research, but shows failed-run feedback beats aggregate score alone.

records.title: LProp: Propagating Latent Uncertainty through Evidence-Conditioned Belief Revision in LLM Agents
records.claim: We introduce Latent Uncertainty, a latent-space estimator that preserves uncertainty-relevant information without lengthy descriptions.

method_and_setup.method: We introduce Latent Uncertainty, a latent-space estimator that preserves uncertainty-relevant information without lengthy descriptions.

records.change_for_agents: Carry uncertainty with intermediate agent judgments and revise it when new evidence arrives.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Relevant to multi-step agents passing tentative judgments downstream as facts; a latent uncertainty approach, not yet something to adopt.

records.title: ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents
records.claim: We propose ARISE (Agent Refinement through Iterative Self-Evaluation), a practical memory architecture in which the agent's memory evolves from its own failures without updating model weights, tools, or workflow logic.

method_and_setup.method: We propose ARISE (Agent Refinement through Iterative Self-Evaluation), a practical memory architecture in which the agent's memory evolves from its own failures without updating model weights, tools, or workflow logic.

results.measures: ARISE-Teacher uses 4.0% fewer model calls and 5.2% fewer output tokens at comparable per-task cost (-1.0%).

records.change_for_agents: Accept a new memory rule only if held-out accuracy rises.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Memory that learns from failures as retrievable micro notes plus consolidated rules, with a held-out accuracy gate, without touching weights or tools; maps onto an agent memory file workflow.

records.title: RefinementGuard: Counterexample-Directed Semantic Qualification for Hidden Agent-Tool Execution
records.claim: We introduce RefinementGuard: translation validation for hidden, effectful agent-tool lowerings, coupled to artifact-bound, fail-closed runtime admission.

method_and_setup.method: We introduce RefinementGuard: translation validation for hidden, effectful agent-tool lowerings, coupled to artifact-bound, fail-closed runtime admission.

results.measures: Among 100 activated, non-equivalent development/qualification faults adjudicated by one human, parent-semantic validation rejects 49/100 (operator-cluster bootstrap 95% CI [33.7%, 64.8%]).

The objective is selective admission, not maximum mutation rejection: exact equality rejects 100/100 faults but also all 60 valid variants, whereas obligation-based validation accepts 60/60; its 51 re
On a frozen disjoint input split, the held-out B2-B3 result is localization-only because 21 patch mutants fail structurally; B3 rejects 38/56 localization defects.

records.change_for_agents: Validate a rewritten tool-call graph against a reference on isolated state before letting it run, and fail closed.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Relevant to tool runtimes that rewrite agent operations into parallel graphs; shows validating the lowering before admitting it.

records.title: Thinking Fast, Anywhere: One System-1 for the Decision Points of Any Agent Workflow
records.claim: We present AnyS1, a framework that turns human-authored procedural skills, whose instructions naturally specify where choices arise and which options apply, into a shared, domain-general source of decision points.

method_and_setup.method: We present AnyS1, a framework that turns human-authored procedural skills, whose instructions naturally specify where choices arise and which options apply, into a shared, domain-general source of decision points.

results.measures: Across three unseen benchmarks and distinct System-2 model families, AnyS1 preserves task reliability while cutting episode cost by 75-91% and model-call time by 63-92% relative to an uncompiled Syste

records.change_for_agents: Use skill instructions to find enumerable decision points and send them to a small model.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Uses skills as the source of decision points to route cheap steps to a small model; relevant to cutting cost of skill-driven agents.

records.title: Continual Tool-Space Extension Learning for Multimodal Agents
records.claim: This work proposes COTEX, continual tool-space extension learning, that adds new tools at efficient adapter-level cost.

method_and_setup.method: This work proposes COTEX, continual tool-space extension learning, that adds new tools at efficient adapter-level cost.

records.change_for_agents: Add new tools through small adapters instead of retraining the whole agent.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Adding new tools to an agent at adapter-level cost without retraining everything; mainly multimodal, so low direct relevance.

records.title: Metrics-in-the-Loop: Complexity Feedback Reshapes Agent-Written Code
records.claim: We introduce metrics-in-the-loop, an inference-time intervention that gives agents in-flight feedback: cheap, automatically computed code metrics injected into the agent's context during the trajectory.

method_and_setup.method: We introduce metrics-in-the-loop, an inference-time intervention that gives agents in-flight feedback: cheap, automatically computed code metrics injected into the agent's context during the trajectory.

records.change_for_agents: Inject automatically computed code metrics into the agent context during the run.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Cheap code metrics injected into the agent context mid-trajectory is something a Claude Code hook could do today.

records.title: SCAFFOLD: Toward Warrant-Preserving Evidence Transport for Reusable LLM-Agent Skills
records.claim: The paper sharpens this position through Warrant-Preserving Evidence Transport (WPET), a proposed discipline for deciding which historical evidence remains admissible after context change.

method_and_setup.method: The paper sharpens this position through Warrant-Preserving Evidence Transport (WPET), a proposed discipline for deciding which historical evidence remains admissible after context change.

records.change_for_agents: Record the context an observation was made in and re-check it before reusing it in a skill.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Raises when evidence recorded in a skill or memory stays valid after context changes; a position paper, relevant to stale skill files.

records.title: Reducing Inference Cost of Coding Agents with Timeout Cascades
records.claim: We evaluate 36 popular large and small open-weight models released since 2024 on a software engineering benchmark, and find that recent small models are closing the accuracy gap compared to their large counterparts.

method_and_setup.method: We evaluate 36 popular large and small open-weight models released since 2024 on a software engineering benchmark, and find that recent small models are closing the accuracy gap compared to their large counterparts.

results.measures: Following this observation, we show that by utilizing a hybrid inference strategy that tries a small model first and escalates to a large one only when needed, we can achieve up to 33% reduction in to

records.change_for_agents: Try a cheap small model first with a timeout, and escalate to a larger model only on failure.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Small open-weight models closing the gap on SWE tasks and a timeout-cascade idea matter for running local coding agents on 64 GB.

records.title: automodel: A Skill for Agentic Model Discovery
records.claim: We present automodel, an agent skill for general model discovery.

method_and_setup.method: We present automodel, an agent skill for general model discovery.

records.change_for_agents: Package model discovery as an agent skill rather than a hand-run search.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: An agent skill for finding models; a concrete skill-file example to learn from or install.

records.title: Semantic Context Handoff with On-Demand Evidence for Long-Horizon Agents
records.claim: We introduce Semantic Context Handoff (SCH), whose central abstraction is state--evidence separation: a compact semantic state carries the agent's current interpretation, while supporting action--observation evidence remains separately addressable and can re-enter context when later execution makes it relevant, without separate summarization or retrieval-model calls.

method_and_setup.method: We introduce Semantic Context Handoff (SCH), whose central abstraction is state--evidence separation: a compact semantic state carries the agent's current interpretation, while supporting action--observation evidence remains separately addressable and can re-enter context when later execution makes it relevant, without separate summarization or retrieval-model calls.

results.measures: In the complete-system comparison, SCH achieves 86.9% Pass@1 while using 43% fewer tokens and 41% less wall-clock time than the strongest baseline by task performance.

records.change_for_agents: Hand off a compact semantic state and keep raw action/observation evidence retrievable on demand.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: State/evidence separation for handing context between steps or sessions fits long-horizon agent handoffs.

records.title: MoE-Context: Show the Model Only What It Needs
records.claim: AI agents read their whole history at every step.

method_and_setup.method: AI agents read their whole history at every step.

records.change_for_agents: Mask irrelevant context blocks in the KV cache rather than deleting and re-prefilling.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Hides context blocks by masking over a single KV cache instead of removing them; relevant to local inference and context assembly.

records.title: Resolution as Attention for Efficient Agent Memory Perception
records.claim: Motivated by this insight, we propose Resolution as Attention (RAA), a memory perception mechanism that uses visual resolution as a means of attention allocation across interaction histories.

method_and_setup.method: Motivated by this insight, we propose Resolution as Attention (RAA), a memory perception mechanism that uses visual resolution as a means of attention allocation across interaction histories.

results.measures: Experiments across multiple tasks and backbones show that RAA reduces token consumption by over 50% without compromising task performance.

records.change_for_agents: Show past interactions at lower resolution unless they are relevant to the next decision.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Renders past interactions as images at variable resolution to cut tokens by over 50%; an unusual memory compression idea for multimodal agents.

records.title: Local AI Agents in Power Electronics Simulation: Deployment, Measurements and Costs
records.claim: To address this gap, a systematic evaluation framework is presented in this paper.

method_and_setup.method: To address this gap, a systematic evaluation framework is presented in this paper.

records.change_for_agents: Measure local agent deployment cost against hosted before choosing.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: A measured local-agent deployment in a niche domain; useful as a data point on local deployment cost.

records.title: When Single Agent Is Enough: Rethinking Multi-Agent Systems for Automated Code Review
records.claim: Prior work has proposed techniques for Review Comment Generation (RCG) and Code Refinement (CR), with recent Multi-Agent (MA) approaches achieving state-of-the-art results by coordinating agents specialized in different quality dimensions.

method_and_setup.method: Prior work has proposed techniques for Review Comment Generation (RCG) and Code Refinement (CR), with recent Multi-Agent (MA) approaches achieving state-of-the-art results by coordinating agents specialized in different quality dimensions.

records.change_for_agents: Baseline a single agent before adding multi-agent coordination.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Checks whether multi-agent coordination beats a single agent for code review; relevant to when not to use multi-agent.

records.title: Dependency Fabrication in Repository Deployment Agents
records.claim: On MinimalSetupAgent, which was built for this report, mitigations proposed in the reward-hacking literature were most effective when the agent received a direct rule and had a clear way to stop and report the problem.

method_and_setup.method: On MinimalSetupAgent, which was built for this report, mitigations proposed in the reward-hacking literature were most effective when the agent received a direct rule and had a clear way to stop and report the problem.

records.change_for_agents: Give agents an explicit rule and a clear stop-and-report path for unresolvable dependencies.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Fabricated dependencies in repository-deployment agents, with mitigations that worked when the agent had a direct rule and a way to stop and report.

records.title: Repository-Grounded Rubrics for Execution-Free Evaluation of Coding Agents
records.claim: We adapt agentic rubrics, introduced for selecting among candidate patches, into an execution-free measure of how far a patch satisfies a task's requirements.

method_and_setup.method: We adapt agentic rubrics, introduced for selecting among candidate patches, into an execution-free measure of how far a patch satisfies a task's requirements.

records.change_for_agents: Grade patches against repository-grounded rubrics when you cannot run tests.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Execution-free rubric scoring of patches is a cheap way to grade coding agent output.

records.title: Idempotency Is Not Recovery: A Fault-Injection Study of Language-Model Agent Tool Actions
records.claim: We study these failure modes in a controlled agent runtime combining authorization, an action ledger, target-side idempotency, reconciliation, and evidence sealing.

method_and_setup.method: We study these failure modes in a controlled agent runtime combining authorization, an action ledger, target-side idempotency, reconciliation, and evidence sealing.

results.measures: In 200 known original crash and replay pairs, the full configuration recorded 0/200 repeated effects versus 117/200 for each simpler baseline.
A ledger-related ablation had 170/170 orphaned effects versus 0/170 and 200/300 recovery successes versus 300/300 for the full configuration.
Disabling reconciliation left 100/100 known post-effect crash outcomes ambiguous despite no observed duplicates.

records.change_for_agents: Keep an action ledger and reconcile after failures instead of relying on idempotent retries alone.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Idempotency is not recovery: directly relevant to an agent taking real actions (action ledger, reconciliation) for a day-admin agent.

records.title: The Value Semantics Layer: Enabling Machine-Understandable Databases for Agentic AI
records.claim: Existing metadata systems expose schemas, catalogs, lineage, and governance information, but provide limited support for representing operational semantics.

method_and_setup.method: Existing metadata systems expose schemas, catalogs, lineage, and governance information, but provide limited support for representing operational semantics.

records.change_for_agents: Expose value semantics of database columns to the planner as persistent metadata.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Persistent planner-visible value semantics for databases; relevant to agents querying app data (e.g. Supabase).

records.title: Safe Personal RSI: Evaluating and Repairing Personal-Agent Updates
records.claim: We study Safe Personal RSI, an update-evaluation component developed for Kicker.

method_and_setup.method: We study Safe Personal RSI, an update-evaluation component developed for Kicker.

results.measures: In repair confirmation, an admitted GPT-5.6 Luna repair reduces attack violations from 10.7% to 0% and increases safe task completion from 89.7% to 100%; a broad handwritten authority rule matches the
Under stronger attacks, a repair transferred from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to Qwen3-14B reduces violations from 69.0% to 17.9% and increases safe task completion from 19.5% to 64.4%.

records.change_for_agents: Evaluate each personal-agent self-update against a regression set and repair before applying.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Evaluating and repairing personal-agent updates before they ship is close to Mitamaton-style personal agents.

records.title: Learning through Discernment: when a small language model learns from user feedback on the job, and when it decays
records.claim: We study a small model (Qwen3 0.6B and 1.7B) with a LoRA adapter, fine-tuned each night on the attempts a judge accepts, over 127 lives of up to a year on WebShop and $τ^2$-bench.

method_and_setup.method: We study a small model (Qwen3 0.6B and 1.7B) with a LoRA adapter, fine-tuned each night on the attempts a judge accepts, over 127 lives of up to a year on WebShop and $τ^2$-bench.

results.measures: When the user cannot see the outcome ($τ^2$-bench), the sense read reactions correctly, yet 80% of its lessons were failures the customer had thanked.

records.change_for_agents: Fine-tune a small adapter nightly on judge-accepted attempts.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Nightly LoRA on a 0.6B/1.7B model from accepted attempts: a local-model continual-learning pattern.

records.title: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?
records.claim: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents are widely trained in executable GUI environments.

method_and_setup.method: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents are widely trained in executable GUI environments.

results.measures: Pruning unneeded features instead raises success from 51.61% to 56.13%, entirely on tasks whose environments it left unchanged.
It outperforms Full in the full environment (55.48% versus 51.61% success) with lower construction cost.

records.change_for_agents: Keep reward and data coverage complete and prune other environment features.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Shows what a GUI-agent training environment can drop; relevant to mobile/computer-use agents.

records.title: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents
records.claim: We evaluate benign over-reach with one pair of models, not adversarial planners.

method_and_setup.method: We evaluate benign over-reach with one pair of models, not adversarial planners.

results.measures: When the planner adds work the user never asked for, contracts complete the user's task in 27/30 runs and the intent-visible reviewer in 16/30, because a reviewer can only refuse a whole command.
They are indistinguishable from blind review, and once the benchmark's environment terms are clarified, every condition that changes state hits a wrong target in 40-49% of those runs.

records.change_for_agents: Grant only the tools a declared intent needs.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Removing tools from agents via intent contracts maps directly to scoping MCP/tool permissions per task.

records.title: AutoPI: Taxonomy-Guided Adaptive Red Teaming for Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
records.claim: We present AutoPI, an adaptive red teamer designed to find many different ways to break a target, not just to break it often.

method_and_setup.method: We present AutoPI, an adaptive red teamer designed to find many different ways to break a target, not just to break it often.

results.measures: On AgentDojo, AutoPI finds a successful injection against Qwen3.6-35B in all six classes of the taxonomy and for more than 90% of its techniques.
Against Claude Haiku 5.5, the most robust target we evaluate, it achieves between 20% and 50% higher ASR and between 25% and 400% higher class-level coverage than recent state-of-the-art adaptive red

records.change_for_agents: Red-team for diversity of attack types, not only attack success rate.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Adaptive taxonomy-guided red teaming for agents finds diverse breaks; useful for testing a tool-using agent.

records.title: PIPETTE: Prompt Injection Purple-Teaming for Robust LLM Agents
records.claim: However, we show that achieving high ASR during red-teaming does not guarantee robustness gains from subsequent adversarial training.

method_and_setup.method: However, we show that achieving high ASR during red-teaming does not guarantee robustness gains from subsequent adversarial training.

records.change_for_agents: Do not use attack success rate alone to choose red-team data for hardening.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: High attack success in red-teaming does not guarantee robustness after adversarial training; matters for how to harden agents.

records.title: Probing agent overeagerness in realistic settings with continuation audits
records.claim: We introduce Continuation Audits, a pipeline that grounds the auditor on a prefix drawn from a real coding-agent transcript and directs it to continue the trajectory toward a seeded behaviour.

method_and_setup.method: We introduce Continuation Audits, a pipeline that grounds the auditor on a prefix drawn from a real coding-agent transcript and directs it to continue the trajectory toward a seeded behaviour.

records.change_for_agents: Audit agents by continuing real transcript prefixes toward a seeded behaviour.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Continuation audits probe reckless agent actions from real transcript prefixes, usable with open-weight models.

records.title: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview Technical Report
records.claim: We introduce Clover-35B-A3B-Preview (Clover), a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35 billion total parameters and 3 billion activated parameters, supporting thinking-mode generation.

method_and_setup.method: We introduce Clover-35B-A3B-Preview (Clover), a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35 billion total parameters and 3 billion activated parameters, supporting thinking-mode generation.

results.measures: On internal agent workloads, it reaches a reported generation speed of 680 tokens/s using one NVIDIA GB300 GPU at BF16 precision and batch size one.
On an internal set of 500 groups, joint prediction raises question accuracy from 90.37% to 93.88% and all-correct group accuracy from 65.4% to 77.0%.

records.change_for_agents: Watch for open weights and runtime support before testing it locally.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: A 35B/3B-active diffusion language model with strong agent benchmark numbers; fit on 64 GB unified memory depends on quantization and diffusion runtime support, not stated in the abstract.

records.title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses
records.claim: We introduce Agentic Harness Engineering Beta (AHE-Beta), a requirement-centered loop that brings real-world engineering practices into harness evolution.

method_and_setup.method: We introduce Agentic Harness Engineering Beta (AHE-Beta), a requirement-centered loop that brings real-world engineering practices into harness evolution.

results.measures: Empirically, on held-out tasks, AHE-Beta raises pass@1 from 21.9% to 33.3% while using 40.8% fewer tokens than Base Harness, and achieves higher pass@1 than Claude Code, Meta-Harness, and AHE.
Without further evolution, the gains transfer to GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with pass@1 improvements of 15.8% and 5.3% over Base Harness.

records.change_for_agents: Drive harness changes from simulated multi-turn user requirements, not only benchmark scores.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Evolving agent harnesses from simulated user requirements rather than benchmark scores fits Claude Code harness/skill tuning.
